cities.name: Paris
cities.summary: France's capital pairs world-class museums, grand boulevards and river views with neighborhood cafés, markets and late-night energy.

cities.name: Versailles
cities.summary: Best known for the palace of Louis XIV, Versailles rewards a day or overnight stay with lavish interiors, formal gardens and elegant streets.

clusters.name: Market Quarter and Potager du Roi

cities.name: Strasbourg
cities.summary: Strasbourg blends Alsatian timbered lanes, a soaring Gothic cathedral and a lively food scene with a distinctly European outlook.

cities.name: Colmar
cities.summary: Colmar is a compact Alsace favorite of canals, painted gables and excellent wine bars, with easy access to nearby vineyard villages.

cities.name: Lyon
cities.summary: Lyon combines Roman roots, Renaissance lanes and one of France's best dining scenes, all set between two rivers and two hills.

cities.name: Nice
cities.summary: Nice offers Riviera beaches, a handsome old town and big-name art museums, with easy train links along the Côte d'Azur.

cities.name: Cannes
cities.summary: Cannes is more than red carpets: expect polished beaches, island excursions, old-quarter viewpoints and a glamorous Riviera atmosphere.

cities.name: Marseille
cities.summary: France's oldest city mixes Mediterranean grit and energy with seafood, historic quarters, islands and dramatic calanques.

cities.name: Bordeaux
cities.summary: Bordeaux pairs elegant riverfront architecture with serious wine culture, lively markets and easy excursions into famous vineyard country.

cities.name: Toulouse
cities.summary: The Pink City charms with brick squares, Romanesque treasures, canal walks and one of Europe's strongest aerospace stories.

cities.name: Avignon
cities.summary: Avignon's papal palace, medieval walls and Provençal squares make a rewarding base for culture, food and Rhône valley wine trips.

clusters.name: Palace of the Popes and Bridge

cities.name: Chamonix
cities.summary: Chamonix is one of Europe's classic alpine bases, prized for Mont Blanc views, cable cars, glacier access and year-round outdoor adventure.

cities.name: Mont Saint-Michel
cities.summary: The abbey-crowned tidal mount is one of France's signature sights, especially atmospheric early or late in the day once day-trippers thin out.

cities.name: Loire Valley
cities.summary: A castle-rich stretch of central France, the Loire Valley excels at Renaissance châteaux, gardens, wine tasting and gentle cycling.

cities.name: Zurich
cities.summary: Zurich mixes polished lakefront scenery, a compact old town, excellent museums and easy rail access to the rest of Switzerland.

cities.name: Lucerne
cities.summary: Lucerne is a classic Swiss stop for lakeside scenery, covered bridges, mountain excursions and a beautifully preserved old town.

cities.name: Interlaken
cities.summary: Interlaken sits between two lakes and works brilliantly as a base for alpine rail trips, cruises and adventure sports.

cities.name: Grindelwald
cities.summary: Grindelwald delivers big Eiger views, lift-linked hikes and winter sports in one of the Bernese Oberland's best-known villages.

cities.name: Lauterbrunnen
cities.summary: Lauterbrunnen's vertical valley of cliffs and waterfalls is one of Switzerland's most dramatic landscapes and a gateway to high villages.

cities.name: Bern
cities.summary: Switzerland's capital charms with arcaded medieval streets, river bends, strong museums and a relaxed local feel.

cities.name: Geneva
cities.summary: Geneva combines lakefront elegance, major international institutions and an old town packed with history and good dining.

clusters.name: International Geneva
attractions: International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum

cities.name: Montreux
cities.summary: Montreux is a polished Lake Geneva resort backed by vineyards and Alps, with one of Switzerland's best lakeside promenades.

cities.name: Zermatt
cities.summary: Car-free Zermatt is the Matterhorn base for iconic viewpoints, high lifts, polished chalets and some of the Alps' best mountain scenery.

cities.name: St. Moritz
cities.summary: St. Moritz is Switzerland at its glossiest, mixing high-alpine panoramas, lake views, winter sports and grand-hotel polish.

cities.name: Basel
cities.summary: Basel stands out for top-tier art, a walkable old town and lively Rhine-side summer culture at the meeting point of three countries.

cities.name: Engelberg
cities.summary: Engelberg is a convenient central Swiss resort for monastery history, mountain lifts and family-friendly alpine activities.

cities.name: Jungfraujoch
cities.summary: The Top of Europe station brings high-alpine glaciers, observatory views and snow experiences within reach by rail and cable car.

cities.name: Mount Titlis
cities.summary: Mount Titlis is a high-value Swiss mountain day for glacier scenery, a rotating cable car and easy all-season snow fun.

cities.name: Luxembourg City
cities.summary: Luxembourg City blends dramatic fortifications, polished squares and modern institutions in a compact capital easy to explore on foot.

clusters.name: Squares and National Collections
attractions: National Museum of History and Art

cities.name: Vianden
cities.summary: Vianden is a storybook riverside town crowned by one of Europe's finest hilltop castles and surrounded by wooded Ardennes scenery.

cities.name: Echternach
cities.summary: Luxembourg's oldest town combines an abbey heritage core with quick access to the rocky trails and streams of Mullerthal.

cities.name: Clervaux
cities.summary: Clervaux is a quiet Ardennes town known for its castle museums, abbey skyline and green northern Luxembourg setting.

clusters.name: Castle Museums and Town Core
attractions: Museum of the Battle of the Bulge

clusters.name: Abbey and Ardennes Countryside
attractions: Abbey of St Maurice and St Maur

cities.name: Remich
cities.summary: Remich is a pleasant Moselle wine town for river promenades, cellar visits and easy side trips to Schengen and nearby vineyards.

cities.name: Brussels
cities.summary: Belgium's capital mixes ornate squares, strong museums, comic-book culture, beer bars and European institutions in one compact city.

clusters.name: Royal Quarter and Museums
attractions: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

cities.name: Bruges
cities.summary: Bruges is Belgium's fairy-tale classic for canals, belfry views, cobbled lanes and a richly preserved medieval center.

cities.name: Ghent
cities.summary: Ghent feels youthful and lively, pairing medieval quays and major art treasures with bars, students and strong local food.

cities.name: Antwerp
cities.summary: Antwerp stands out for fashion, diamonds, major art collections and a handsome old center balanced by a creative, modern edge.

cities.name: Leuven
cities.summary: Leuven is a compact university city with Gothic highlights, famous beer ties and a youthful café scene centered on lively squares.

cities.name: Mechelen
cities.summary: Mechelen is an underrated stop between Brussels and Antwerp, with a grand cathedral, canal walks and strong historic character.

cities.name: Liège
cities.summary: Liège offers gritty character, hilltop stairways, lively markets and a mix of Walloon history, riverfront walks and late-night energy.
